name: Moderation
description: Ban, unban, kick and mute commands, limited to members with the matching permission.
about: The template adds four slash commands: /ban, /unban, /kick and /mute. Each one takes the user and an optional reason, which shows up in your server's audit log. /mute also takes a number of seconds and uses Discord's timeout, so the member can't send messages or join voice channels until it runs out.

Discord only shows each command to members with the matching permission: Ban Members for /ban and /unban, Kick Members for /kick and Timeout Members for /mute. The bot confirms each action in a reply only the moderator sees, and /ban also deletes the user's messages from the last hour.

faq.question: Who can use the moderation commands?
faq.answer: Only members with the matching permission, like Ban Members for /ban. You can change who sees each command per role or channel under Integrations in your server settings.

faq.question: How long can I mute someone for?
faq.answer: Up to 28 days, which is 2,419,200 seconds. That's the longest timeout Discord allows.

faq.question: What permissions does the bot need?
faq.answer: Ban Members, Kick Members and Timeout Members. Keep the bot's role above the roles of the members it moderates, since that's how Discord decides who a bot can act on.

faq.question: Can I change the replies or log actions to a channel?
faq.answer: Yes. Once added, the commands are normal Kite commands. Open one in the editor to change its reply, or add a Send message block that posts each action to a log channel.

name: AI Automod
description: AI deletes spam, scams, ads and insults and logs them for your moderators.
about: The bot checks every message with AI, also when it's edited, and deletes spam, scams, unwanted ads and insults. Every message it deletes is posted in your log channel with who sent it and where.

The AI only deletes a message when it's at least 90% sure that it breaks the rules. Messages it's less sure about stay up and go to the log channel with a link, so a moderator can decide. You can add rules of your own, like no links to other servers, and they're checked together with the default ones.

Each check costs 1 credit. On a busy server, set New Member Days to a number, like 7, so only members who joined within that many days are checked. Spam bots and raiders are usually new to the server, so that catches most of them for a fraction of the credits. Members who can manage messages, like your moderators, are never checked.

faq.question: Which AI model does it use?
faq.answer: Jev by TypeSafe, a model made for decisions instead of chat. It answers with how likely it is that a message breaks the rules, and the AI Check block compares that with its thresholds.

faq.question: How many credits does it use?
faq.answer: 1 credit for every message it checks, and again when a message is edited. Messages without text and messages of moderators are skipped. To check fewer messages, set New Member Days to check only members who joined within that many days. Deleting a message and posting it in the log channel cost 1 credit each.

faq.question: Can the AI make mistakes?
faq.answer: Yes. The AI Check block deletes a message when the AI is at least 90% sure it breaks the rules, sends it to your moderators between 50% and 90%, and ignores it below 50%. Change the yes threshold to delete more or fewer messages, and the no threshold to review more or fewer. The no threshold can't be above the yes threshold.

faq.question: Can it time out members?
faq.answer: Not out of the box. Add a Timeout member block after the block that deletes the message, so members whose message the AI deletes are timed out too.

faq.question: What permissions does the bot need?
faq.answer: Manage Messages in the channels it checks, and Send Messages and Embed Links in the log channel.

faq.question: Do I need the Message Content Intent?
faq.answer: Yes. Turn it on under Bot in the Discord Developer Portal, or the bot can't read the messages it checks.

setup: Turn on the Message Content Intent under Bot in the Discord Developer Portal, so the bot can read the messages.

name: Ask AI
description: Members ask AI questions with /ask or by mentioning the bot.
about: Members ask the AI a question with /ask, and only they see the answer. They can also mention the bot in a message, and it replies to that message in the channel for everyone to read.

The system prompt setting gives the AI its personality and rules, like the topics it should stick to or the language it should answer in. Leave it empty for a general assistant. Answers use the Fast AI model, and the 10,000 monthly credits of the free plan cover more than 1,400 of them.

faq.question: Which AI model does it use?
faq.answer: The Fast model tier. You can switch the AI block to Balanced or Smartest in the editor, which gives better answers and costs more credits per answer.

faq.question: Does the bot read every message?
faq.answer: No. The event listener only runs for messages that mention the bot, so other messages are never sent to the AI.

faq.question: Can I keep the AI on topic?
faq.answer: Yes. Describe in the system prompt what the AI should help with and how it should answer, for example only questions about your game or your server's rules.

faq.question: Do I need the Message Content Intent?
faq.answer: No. Discord includes the text of messages that mention your bot even when the intent is off.

name: Welcomer
description: Greets new members in a channel you choose, and says goodbye when they leave.
about: Whenever someone joins your server, the bot posts a message that mentions them in the channel you pick. It's a normal Send message block, so you can change the text or turn it into an embed with the member's avatar. When a member leaves, it posts a goodbye in the same channel. Uncheck the leave listener if you only want welcomes.
To see new members, your bot needs the Server Members Intent. It's one switch under Bot in the Discord Developer Portal.

faq.question: What does the bot need to welcome members?
faq.answer: The Server Members Intent, which you turn on under Bot in the Discord Developer Portal, and permission to send messages in the welcome channel.

faq.question: Can I welcome members with a DM instead?
faq.answer: Yes. Replace the Send message block with a direct message block in the editor, or keep both.

faq.question: Can new members get a role too?
faq.answer: Yes. Add an Add role to member block after the message. If members should click a button before they get the role, use the Verification template instead.

name: Verification
description: Posts a message with a Verify button that gives new members a role, so they have to click it before they see the rest of the server.
about: When you add the template, Kite posts a message with a Verify button in the channel you pick. Members who click it get the role you chose, and the bot tells them in a reply only they see that they can now see the rest of the server.

To keep new members out until they verify, hide your channels from @everyone and let the verified role see them. The verification channel itself has to stay visible to everyone. The message is a message template, so its button keeps working for as long as the message exists, and you can change it and send it again under Message Templates.

faq.question: What does the bot need to give the role?
faq.answer: A role above the verified role. Discord lets bots give the roles below their own highest role, so move the bot's role up once in your server settings.

faq.question: How does it help against spam accounts?
faq.answer: New accounts can't see or post in your channels until they click Verify, so spam that relies on joining and posting right away doesn't reach your members. You can add Discord's own verification level in your server settings on top.

faq.question: Can I post the message again?
faq.answer: Yes. Open Message Templates in your app and send the Verification message to any channel.

name: Suggestions
description: A /suggest command that posts suggestions to a channel for members to vote on.
about: Members use /suggest to post an idea in the suggestions channel you pick. The bot posts it as an embed with their name and avatar, then adds 👍 and 👎 reactions so everyone can vote. The member gets a reply only they see, with a link to the channel.
Each member can suggest something once a minute, so the channel doesn't get spammed. You can change that in the Command Cooldown block of the command.

faq.question: What permissions does the bot need?
faq.answer: View Channel, Send Messages, Embed Links and Add Reactions in the suggestions channel.

faq.question: Can members suggest anonymously?
faq.answer: Yes. Open the command in the editor and remove the author from the embed of the Send message block.

faq.question: Can I stop members from writing in the suggestions channel?
faq.answer: Yes. Take away Send Messages for @everyone in the channel. The bot still posts there as long as its own role can send messages.

faq.question: How do I change the cooldown?
faq.answer: Open /suggest in the editor and change the seconds in the Command Cooldown block, up to one hour, or delete the block to remove the cooldown.

name: Starboard
description: Posts messages that get enough ⭐ reactions to a starboard channel.
about: When a message gets the number of ⭐ reactions you choose, the bot posts it in the starboard channel with its author, its text and a button to jump to it. Every new star after that updates the count on the starboard post, so a message is only posted once.

Only stars in the server of the starboard channel count, and not the ones in the starboard channel itself. The emoji is set in the event filter of the listener, so you can use a different one, including a custom emoji of your server.

faq.question: What permissions does the bot need?
faq.answer: View Channel and Read Message History in the channels members star messages in, and Send Messages and Embed Links in the starboard channel.

faq.question: Can I use a different emoji than ⭐?
faq.answer: Yes. Open the event listener and change the emoji of the Event Filter block. It takes a standard emoji or the name of a custom emoji.

faq.question: Do I need the Message Content Intent?
faq.answer: Yes, or the starboard posts show no text. Turn it on under Bot in the Discord Developer Portal.

faq.question: What happens if someone removes their star?
faq.answer: The post stays in the starboard. Its count is updated the next time someone adds a star.

name: Server Info
about: /avatar shows a user's avatar in full size. /userinfo shows their ID, when they created their account and joined the server, their highest role and how many roles they have. Both show the member who uses them, unless they pick another user.
/serverinfo shows the server's owner, member count, creation date, number of channels and roles, and boosts. /userinfo and /serverinfo only work in servers, so Discord hides them in DMs.

faq.question: Does the bot need any permissions?
faq.answer: No. The commands reply to the interaction, so the bot doesn't need to send messages in the channel, and it needs no privileged intents.

faq.question: Can I show more info about a user?
faq.answer: Yes. Open /userinfo in the editor and add fields to the embed. The placeholder picker lists everything Kite knows about a member, like their nickname, role color or whether they're boosting.

faq.question: Why does /userinfo say "Not in this server"?
faq.answer: The picked user isn't a member of the server, so there's no join date or roles to show.

name: Modmail
description: Users DM the bot to reach your staff, and staff answer with /reply.
about: Members send your bot a direct message, and the bot posts it in your staff channel with a mention of the member and their user ID. The member gets a confirmation that the staff team received it.

Staff answer with /reply, picking the member and writing the message. The bot sends the reply to the member as a direct message and posts it in the channel, so the rest of the staff can see the message was answered. Only members with the Manage Messages permission see /reply.

faq.question: What happens when a reply can't be delivered?
faq.answer: /reply tells the staff member right away, for example when the member turned off DMs, so nobody waits for a reply that never arrived.

faq.question: Can I change the messages?
faq.answer: Yes. The message posted for the staff and the confirmation the member gets are normal blocks, so you can change their text or turn them into embeds in the editor.

faq.question: Who can answer modmail?
faq.answer: Everyone with the Manage Messages permission can use /reply, and you can change that per role under Integrations in your server settings.

name: Counting
description: A counting channel where members count up one number at a time, and start over when someone gets it wrong.
about: Members take turns posting the next number in the counting channel you pick, as a number or as math like 5 + 5. The bot reacts with ✅ to every correct number. If someone posts the wrong number, or two numbers in a row, the bot says who ruined it and the count starts again at 1. Messages that aren't a number or math are ignored, so members can still chat.
The count and who counted last are kept in a stored variable for each channel, so it survives restarts. To count in more channels, add them to the channel check at the top of the event listener.

faq.question: What permissions does the bot need?
faq.answer: View Channel, Read Message History, Send Messages and Add Reactions in the counting channel.

faq.question: Does the bot need the Message Content Intent?
faq.answer: Yes. Turn it on under Bot in the Discord Developer Portal, or the bot can't read the numbers members post.

faq.question: What math can members use?
faq.answer: +, -, *, x, ×, /, ÷, % and ^ with parentheses, like (3 * 4) - 2. A message counts if it's only math with a whole number above 0 as result, which has to be the next number. Other messages, like 24/7, are ignored.

faq.question: Can I change the messages or the ✅ reaction?
faq.answer: Yes. They're normal blocks in the event listener, edit the text of the Send message blocks or the emoji of the reaction block.

faq.question: How do I reset the count?
faq.answer: Post a wrong number, or delete the value of the counting variable on the Variables page of your app.

setup: Turn on the Message Content Intent under Bot in the Discord Developer Portal, so the bot can read the numbers.

name: ER:LC
description: Show your ER:LC private server's status and players, and announce messages in it.
about: The template connects your bot to your Emergency Response: Liberty County private server. /status shows the server's name, player count and join code, and /players lists who's online with their team.

/announce shows a message to everyone in the server, like the :m command in the game. Only members with the Manage Server permission see it. Setup is two steps: enable ER:LC under Integrations in your app with your server key, and authorize Kite once so /announce can run commands.

faq.question: Where do I find my server key?
faq.answer: In ER:LC, open the settings of your private server and copy the server key. Paste it under Integrations in your Kite app.

faq.question: Can the bot react to what happens in the game?
faq.answer: Yes. ER:LC can send your bot emergency calls and chat messages that start with ;, so you can build your own in-game commands with a webhook event listener. The ER:LC guide in Kite's docs shows how.

faq.question: Can the bot run other ER:LC commands?
faq.answer: Yes. The Run ER:LC command block runs any command the game accepts, like :kick or :pm. Copy /announce in the editor and change its command.

setup: Enable ER:LC under Integrations and add your server key.
Authorize Kite for your server once, so /announce can run commands.

name: AFK
description: An /afk command that tells members who ping you that you're away, and welcomes you back when you talk again.
about: Members use /afk with an optional reason, like /afk lunch, and the bot confirms it and adds [AFK] in front of their nickname.

When someone pings a member who is AFK, the bot replies with their reason and how long ago they went AFK. As soon as the AFK member sends a message, the bot welcomes them back, removes their AFK and takes [AFK] off their nickname. AFK is per server, so being AFK in one server doesn't show in another.

faq.question: Does the bot ping anyone when it replies?
faq.answer: No. Its replies mention the members by name, but pings are turned off, so the AFK member doesn't get pinged a second time.

faq.question: Why didn't my nickname change?
faq.answer: The bot needs the Manage Nicknames permission, and its role has to be above yours. It can never change the nickname of the server owner. If [AFK] and your nickname together are longer than 32 characters, Discord's limit, the bot leaves your nickname as it is. AFK still works without the nickname.

faq.question: What if a message pings several members?
faq.answer: The bot answers for one of them, skipping the author. Role pings don't count. Replying to a message of an AFK member counts too, unless the reply has its ping turned off.

faq.question: How many credits does it use?
faq.answer: Messages cost nothing unless they come from or ping an AFK member. Using /afk costs up to 3 credits, for saving the AFK, replying and changing the nickname. Coming back costs 3 as well, and each reply about an AFK member costs 1.

name: Giveaways
description: A /giveaway command with an Enter button that picks random winners when it ends, plus a Reroll button.
about: Members with the Manage Server permission start a giveaway with /giveaway, giving the prize, how long it runs, like 30m, 2 hours or 1d 12h, and optionally how many winners to pick and a role members need to enter. The bot posts the giveaway in the channel with an Enter button, and members see how many entered so far when they enter.

When the time is up, the bot picks the winners at random, shows them in the giveaway message and pings them in a reply. Each member can enter once. If a winner doesn't claim the prize, members with the Manage Server permission can click Reroll to pick someone else, who the bot announces in the channel.

faq.question: How long can a giveaway run?
faq.answer: Between 1 minute and 30 days. Write the duration like 30m, 2 hours or 1d 12h.

faq.question: How are the winners picked?
faq.answer: At random from everyone who entered, and nobody can win twice in the same giveaway. Rerolling never picks someone who already won it, also not the winners of earlier rerolls.

faq.question: Who can start giveaways?
faq.answer: Members with the Manage Server permission. You can change who sees /giveaway per role or channel under Integrations in your server settings.

faq.question: Can I limit a giveaway to a role?
faq.answer: Yes. Pick the role in required_role when starting the giveaway, and only members with it can enter.

faq.question: How do I cancel a giveaway?
faq.answer: Delete the giveaway message before it ends. The bot then doesn't pick any winners.

faq.question: How many credits does it use?
faq.answer: Each entry costs 2 credits. Starting a giveaway and picking its winners costs 8 credits in total, and each reroll 3.

name: Sticky Message
description: Keeps a message at the bottom of a channel by posting it again when the channel goes quiet.
about: Pick a channel and the template keeps a message at the bottom of it, like rules for a channel or how to ask for help. When someone sends a message there, the bot waits until no one has written for 3 seconds, then posts the sticky message again and deletes the previous one. A busy conversation only moves it once, after it calms down.

You write the sticky message in the message editor when you add the template, with text, embeds or images, and can change it under Messages any time without opening the flow. It shows up after the next message in the channel.

faq.question: How do I change the sticky message?
faq.answer: Edit the Sticky message under Messages in your app. The next time the bot posts it, it uses the new version.

faq.question: How many credits does it use?
faq.answer: Messages in the sticky channel are free. Each time the bot posts the sticky message again, it costs 3 credits for posting it, remembering it and deleting the old one. A busy conversation only costs that once, after it calms down, and messages in other channels don't run the flow at all.

faq.question: Does it move below messages from other bots?
faq.answer: No, only messages from members make the bot post it again. Messages from bots, like feeds, stay below the sticky message until a member writes.

faq.question: What permissions does the bot need?
faq.answer: Send Messages, Read Message History and Manage Messages in the sticky channel, so it can post the message, check that no one wrote after it and delete the old one.

name: Reminders
description: A /remind command that sends members a reminder in their DMs after the time they pick.
about: Members use /remind with when to remind them, like 30m, 2 hours or 1d 12h, and what to remind them of. The bot confirms the reminder in a reply only they can see, with the exact time it goes off.

When the time is up, the bot sends the reminder in their DMs. If their DMs are closed, it pings them with the reminder in the channel they used /remind in instead. Reminders can be up to 30 days away.

faq.question: How far ahead can I set a reminder?
faq.answer: Between 1 minute and 30 days. Write the time like 30m, 2 hours or 1d 12h.

faq.question: What if my DMs are closed?
faq.answer: The bot pings you with the reminder in the channel you used /remind in.

faq.question: Can other members see my reminders?
faq.answer: No. The confirmation only shows to you and the reminder goes to your DMs, unless your DMs are closed.

faq.question: How many reminders can I set?
faq.answer: Up to 10 can be waiting at a time, and you can set one every 30 seconds. Once a reminder goes off, you can set a new one.

faq.question: How many credits does it use?
faq.answer: 4 credits for each reminder: reading the time, remembering it, confirming it and sending the reminder. Waiting costs nothing.

name: Honeypot
description: A channel that catches spam bots: anyone but staff who sends a message in it gets softbanned and logged.
about: The template posts a warning in a honeypot channel you pick, telling members not to send messages there. Spam bots that post in every channel fall for it. When a member without the Manage Messages permission sends a message in the honeypot channel, the bot softbans them: it bans them, which deletes their messages from the last day, and unbans them right away, so they can rejoin with a new invite.

Before the softban, the bot forwards the message to a log channel you pick and logs who was kicked, with their user ID, when their account was created and when they joined. You can change the warning in the message editor when adding the template, or later under Messages.

faq.question: What is a softban?
faq.answer: A ban followed right away by an unban. It kicks the member and deletes their recent messages, but they aren't banned and can join again with an invite.

faq.question: What happens if a moderator posts in the honeypot channel?
faq.answer: Members with the Manage Messages or Administrator permission are ignored, so moderators can post there. Anyone else whose role is above the bot's, or who owns the server, can't be banned by the bot, so their message is forwarded to the log channel with a note that the bot couldn't softban them.

faq.question: What permissions does the bot need?
faq.answer: Ban Members, with its role above the members it should catch. In the log channel it needs to see the channel and send messages.
